note: Issue 441, patrons.md section 4 (He asks for his need), crown-demands.md section 5. The one thing he wants that the colony can ship him, never his specialty's kind. Agreeing is a promise of a shipment addressed to him, which the PC makes good only by persuading a governor to prepare it (pc.request_shipment) - the Marshal's two letters, with a patron at the far end. The promise is kept on goods that actually left a town inside the term, and keeping it is the deed that banks with the court; agreeing alone banks nothing, and breaking it costs what a refusal would. Unskippable, as his gold letter is: every patron has both. Placeholder prose.

body.text: I find I am in want of {param:resource}, and I am told your colony has it, or could.
{param:amount} of it, inside {param:months} months, would answer. I should not ask for it from anybody else, because I should not be sure of getting it.
I do not know how these things are managed on your side of the water. I imagine you have to ask somebody, and that he has to be persuaded. I leave that to you.
I do not suppose it will be convenient. Very little that I ask of you seems to be.

options.text: and am glad to be of use
and must be honest about the colony's state

options.label: undertake to ship {param:amount} of {param:resource}
options.text: You shall have {param:amount} of {param:resource} inside {param:months} months. I shall write to the town that holds it this week.

options.label: tell him the colony cannot spare it
options.text: The colony cannot spare it this season. I would rather tell you so now than have you wait for a ship that is not coming.
